problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14049072/assets/0221452e6c995bd4d4e027452c9949d57afc181e99d549434fc48ce8e29ced4b.png)

Consider the RC circuit shown above. Given that the charge $q(t)$ of the capacitor at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
q(t)=A{e}^{-5t}+\frac{P}{29}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\frac{Q}{145}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)
$$

where $A,$ $P,$ and $Q$ are constants, find the value of $P+Q.$

*Hint: The voltage drop ${V}_{C}$ across the capacitor is related to its charge by $q=C{V}_{C},$ where $C$ is the capacitance measured in Farads.*
worked_solution:
The diagram shows a series RC circuit with a source electromotive force (EMF) of $10\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\text{V},$ a resistor with resistance $50\,Ω,$ and a capacitor of capacitance $0.004\,\text{F}.$

The current $I,$ measured in amperes, is defined as the rate of flow of charge $q,$ measured in coulombs. 

$$
I=\frac{\text{d}q}{\text{d}t}
$$

Kirchhoff's voltage law states that in a series circuit, the source voltage (EMF) equals the sum of the voltage drops.

In an RC circuit, there are two voltage drops:

- The voltage drop across the resistor is proportional to the current, with a constant of proportionality $R=50\,Ω.$ So,

$$
{V}_{R}=50I=50\,\frac{dq}{dt}.
$$

- The voltage drop across the capacitor is related to its charge by $q=C{V}_{C}.$ Therefore,

$$
{V}_{C}=\frac{q}{0.004}=250q.
$$

Therefore, by Kirchhoff's voltage law, the differential equation governing the amount of charge $q$ on the capacitor is

$$
10\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)=50\,\frac{dq}{dt}+250q,
$$

which gives

$$
\frac{dq}{dt}+5q=\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t).
$$

This is a first-order linear equation with constant coefficients. So, to find the general solution, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

- To find the complementary solution ${q}_{c},$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
\frac{d{q}_{c}}{dt}+5{q}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving using an integration technique, such as separation of variables, we obtain the complementary solution

$$
{q}_{c}(t)=A{e}^{-5t},
$$

where $A$ is a constant of integration.

- Next, we find the particular solution. Note that the right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is sinusoidal with argument $2t.$ So, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal with argument $2t,$ i.e.,

$$
{q}_{p}(t)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{p} & =\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t), \\ \frac{d{q}_{p}}{dt} & =-2\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\end{aligned}
$$

into the inhomogeneous equation and group like terms on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))+5(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ (-2\alpha +5\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+(5\alpha +2\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2\alpha +5\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) \\ 5\alpha +2\beta =\frac{1}{5}\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =\frac{1}{29},\beta =\frac{2}{145}.$ Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{q}_{p}(t)=\frac{1}{29}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\frac{2}{145}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).
$$

Now, since the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution, the general solution in our case is

$$
q(t)={q}_{c}(t)+{q}_{p}(t)=A{e}^{-5t}+\frac{1}{29}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\frac{2}{145}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).
$$

Therefore, we have $P=1,Q=2,$ and

$$
P+Q=1+2=3.
$$

The diagram shows a series RC circuit with a source electromotive force (EMF) of 10cos⁡(2t)V, a resistor with resistance 50Ω, and a capacitor of capacitance 0.004F.

The current I, measured in amperes, is defined as the rate of flow of charge q, measured in coulombs. I=dqdt

Kirchhoff's voltage law states that in a series circuit, the source voltage (EMF) equals the sum of the voltage drops.

In an RC circuit, there are two voltage drops:

  • The voltage drop across the resistor is proportional to the current, with a constant of proportionality R=50Ω. So, VR=50I=50dqdt.

  • The voltage drop across the capacitor is related to its charge by q=CVC. Therefore, VC=q0.004=250q.

Therefore, by Kirchhoff's voltage law, the differential equation governing the amount of charge q on the capacitor is 10cos⁡(2t)=50dqdt+250q, which gives dqdt+5q=15cos⁡(2t).

This is a first-order linear equation with constant coefficients. So, to find the general solution, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

  • To find the complementary solution qc, we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by dqcdt+5qc=0. Solving using an integration technique, such as separation of variables, we obtain the complementary solution qc(t)=Ae−5t, where A is a constant of integration.

  • Next, we find the particular solution. Note that the right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is sinusoidal with argument 2t. So, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal with argument 2t, i.e., qp(t)=αcos⁡(2t)+βsin⁡(2t). To find the values of α and β, we substitute qp=αcos⁡(2t)+βsin⁡(2t),dqpdt=−2αsin⁡(2t)+2βcos⁡(2t), into the inhomogeneous equation and group like terms on the left-hand side: (−2αsin⁡(2t)+2βcos⁡(2t))+5(αcos⁡(2t)+βsin⁡(2t))=15cos⁡(2t)(−2α+5β)sin⁡(2t)+(5α+2β)cos⁡(2t)=15cos⁡(2t) Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations: {−2α+5β=0(equating the coefficients ofsin⁡(2t))5α+2β=15(equating the coefficients ofcos⁡(2t)) Solving this system gives α=129,β=2145. Therefore, the particular solution is qp(t)=129cos⁡(2t)+2145sin⁡(2t).

Now, since the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution, the general solution in our case is q(t)=qc(t)+qp(t)=Ae−5t+129cos⁡(2t)+2145sin⁡(2t).

Therefore, we have P=1,Q=2, and P+Q=1+2=3.
